about: Twelve junior-astronaut competencies. Mission completion is the evidence for learned, practised and proved moments; the Academy manual is a read-only view of that evidence. These are training milestones, not exams or certification.

competencies.title: Life support
competencies.plain: Air, water and food last only when the crew plans for everyone and keeps a reserve. A leak or a new person changes the plan.

learned.evidence: Count crew needs before choosing how to spend commissioning power.

practised.evidence: Forecast air and water while preparing for darkness.
Recount the crew when Ferreira arrives.

proved.evidence: Bring everyone through seven shifts with the life-support margin intact.
Use the two-person home forecast until the travellers return.

competencies.title: Power
competencies.plain: The low polar Sun makes power uneven. Charge only up to the battery limit, then budget storage for the dark.

learned.evidence: See why the low Sun cannot be treated as an unlimited supply.

practised.evidence: Split daylight energy between storage and the station's needs.
Check the eclipse schedule before making a new budget.
Restore only the camera feeder and verify protected services stay powered.

proved.evidence: Protect the five essential eclipse segments and keep a margin.

competencies.title: Thermal control
competencies.plain: The habitat needs heat, while permanently shadowed ground can chill equipment and samples. Keep both inside their safe limits.

learned.evidence: Balance chamber light, heat and water for the first plants.

practised.evidence: Keep the sealed vault protected in permanent shadow.

proved.evidence: Return with the canisters sealed and temperature protected.

competencies.title: Radiation and space weather
competencies.plain: Read the particle warning, shorten exposure, and use the prepared water and crate shielding. A historical storm is a training replay, not Aurora's measured weather.

learned.evidence: Prepare the shelter before the alarm.

practised.evidence: Compare the 2017 replay with the shelter forecast.
Label the 2012 event as a counterfactual exercise.
Hold water and cargo shielding through the particle peak.

proved.evidence: Keep protection through the final exposure sample before moving water.

competencies.title: Food and plant science
competencies.plain: Plants grow through stages and need controlled conditions. Clean, labelled pollen transfers let Alo and Tara carry a traceable line to seeds.

learned.evidence: Plant both cassettes and begin dated care records.

practised.evidence: Plan a clean, compatible pollen route.
Make the reciprocal transfers and record each care day.
Read the interrupted garden's stage record without inventing an earlier bloom.
Compare the cotton plan with the real lunar germination record.

proved.evidence: Count 42 mature seeds and keep 12 for planting, 30 in reserve.
Plant cotton and reconcile the vault inventory.

competencies.title: EVA and suit operations
competencies.plain: Before a Moon walk, check the suit, a buddy, the route and the return reserve. A field discovery matters only if the team gets home safely.

learned.evidence: Prepare the survey and charge each traveller to the right supply ledger.

practised.evidence: Check the next beacon before crossing a blind corner.

proved.evidence: Bring the sealed cargo and crew home with the return reserve.

competencies.title: Navigation
competencies.plain: There is no GPS on this route. Compare measured slopes, bearings and sight lines, then plan for the whole trip home.

learned.evidence: Turn an old map into a current survey plan.

practised.evidence: Use slope and line of sight before committing a turn.

proved.evidence: Choose the surveyed long road with a return reserve.

competencies.title: Rover operations
competencies.plain: The rover has a slope limit, a finite battery and cargo that needs care. A short cut is useful only when every limit passes.

learned.evidence: Compare route distance with the rover's slope limit.

practised.evidence: Carry sealed cargo and verify the latch for departure.

proved.evidence: Provision the 51-hour trip and drive the safe road within reserve.

competencies.title: Communication
competencies.plain: A powered radio is not proof of a working link. Check each line of sight and each relay hop, then verify both local and Earth paths.

learned.evidence: Separate the planned Earth-link cutoff from the sky model.

practised.evidence: Test each mounted beacon before the next corner.
Plan a local repeater chain and a separate Earth leg.

proved.evidence: Verify both links and the exact current response before the summit call.

competencies.title: Lunar science
competencies.plain: The Moon leaves clues in quakes, shadows, ice signals, flashes and eclipses. Use a reference or a second reading before making a claim.

learned.evidence: Compare independent pressure readings after the quake.

practised.evidence: Calibrate against dry and wet references before tagging ice-bearing material.
Check an impact flash with two cameras.

proved.evidence: Record only what the eclipse camera and labelled diagram support.

competencies.title: Teamwork and systems engineering
competencies.plain: A good crew names roles, tests a shared plan and checks back when conditions change. A debrief records causes without blame.

learned.evidence: Assign rehearsal roles and make the first shared record.

practised.evidence: Repair the garden spur and verify steady readings before reopening.
Share the eclipse plan and read back dependencies.
Resolve every name in the shelter roster.

proved.evidence: Credit both teams and reconcile the final home report.

competencies.title: The scientific method
competencies.plain: Make a prediction, observe what happened, and explain the difference. Keep observed facts apart from inferences and unknowns.

learned.evidence: Keep paired plant photos with their conditions.

practised.evidence: Match recorder labels before inferring a story.
File the familiar voice as a question, not proof.

proved.evidence: Reject fixed detector spots and count only verified flashes.

things.text: A reserve is part of the plan, not spare capacity.
A bright polar site can still have a long dark interval.
Shelter choices follow the measured warning and the actual forecast.
Compatible flowers need clean, labelled pollen transfers.
A seed cycle in space takes care and time.
A shallow moonquake can shake equipment, so the crew checks before diagnosing a fault.
Independent readings locate a fault more safely than one alarm.
A repair needs a steady test before service returns.
Plants can complete a seed cycle; Aurora records its own 42-seed harvest and 12/30 split.
A safe lunar route meets both slope and return-reserve limits.
A bright patch needs a calibrated comparison before an ice claim.
Cold-trap cargo stays sealed and protected from extreme cold.
Two views help separate a real impact flash from an artifact.
A cotton seed can be compared with a real lunar germination record.
A fifth crew member changes air and food demand.
Eclipse phases let the crew budget essential power ahead of time.
Solar output has a limit even when the Sun returns.
A diagram explains the ring but is not a measured surface map.
The 2012 event is a historical measurement used for a what-if.
Protection stays in place until the final exposure check.
The Earth path and local relay are different links.
Distance and slope both matter on the long road.
Earth bearing and local line of sight need separate checks.
A useful relay needs a checked chain, not just a powered dish.
